commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. content.content:
I can't reproduce the full quickstart verbatim, but here are its key technical details.

**Endpoint and request**
- `GET https://api-eus.qrypt.com/api/v1/quantum-entropy?size=1`
- Auth header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- Also sends `Accept: application/json` and a custom `User-Agent`. The docs note Cloudflare blocks Python's default `urllib` User-Agent.
- The docs say `size` is in KiB, not bytes, with a valid range of 1 to 512.

**Response format**
- JSON with a `random` array holding one base64 string per KiB requested, and a `size` field.
- Base64-decode the string before use. The docs say it never contains the key itself.

**Deriving an AES-256 key**
- Decode the entropy and keep the first 32 bytes as the key.
- The docs say to test with AES-256-GCM, encrypting and decrypting a sample message.

**Setup**
- Python 3.9+: install `requests`, `cryptography`, and `python-dotenv`.
- Node 20.12+: no dependencies, uses built-in `fetch` and `process.loadEnvFile`.
- Store the token in a `.env` file as `QRYPT_API_KEY`, and add `.env` to `.gitignore`.

**Error codes**
- **400:** size out of range.
- **401:** auth header missing, malformed, or expired.
- **403:** invalid token or exhausted monthly quota. Check the token first.
- **429:** rate limited. Wait 10 seconds or more and don't retry in a loop.
- **500/503:** service busy or erroring. Try again later.

The docs also advise never printing, logging, or committing the token or generated key, and using fresh entropy for each key.

For the full API reference, see docs.qrypt.com/eaas.

content.text:
I generated an AES-256 key from Qrypt quantum entropy, and an AES-256-GCM encrypt/decrypt test with it succeeded. The key couldn't be saved to disk, though, so it only existed while the script ran.

**What the run did** (`qrypt-run quickstart.mjs`):
```
Received 1024 bytes of quantum entropy
AES-256 key: 256 bits, SHA-256 fingerprint d29c31677db65fb0...
AES-256-GCM round trip OK: "Hello from Qrypt quantum entropy!"
Key not saved to disk (EACCES); it was used in memory only
```

**Project files in `/work`:**
- `quickstart.mjs` — Node script with no dependencies. It loads `QRYPT_API_KEY` from `.env` and requests 1 KiB of entropy from `GET https://api-eus.qrypt.com/api/v1/quantum-entropy?size=1`. It decodes the base64 entropy and uses the first 32 bytes as the key. It then encrypts and decrypts a sample message with AES-256-GCM to check the key. Error codes 400, 401, 403, 429 and 5xx each get a clear message.
- `package.json` — `npm start` runs the script through `qrypt-run`.
- `.gitignore` — keeps `.env` and `aes256.key` out of git.

As the quickstart advises, the script never prints the token or the key. It shows only a short SHA-256 fingerprint of the key.

**Why the key wasn't saved:** in this sandbox, `.env` can only be read through `qrypt-run`, which runs the script as a separate `qrypt` user. That user can't write to `/work`. When you run the script somewhere `/work` is writable, it saves the raw 32-byte key to `aes256.key` with owner-only permissions. Otherwise, you could pass the key straight to whatever needs it (a key store or KMS) instead of writing a file. Each run fetches fresh entropy and produces a new key.
